Design Philosophy & Process Our goal is to create thoughtfully designed, enduring buildings and spaces that contribute to a healthy and inspiring environment for our clients and the surrounding community. Our design process begins with a focus on quality over quantity. We produce an appropriately sized, well-tailored design for each project. We make careful use of space and pay attention to the details, maximizing the usefulness and comfort of the building, while minimizing the resources used to create it. During the design process, we work closely with our clients letting their unique ideas and requirements guide us along the path to a correspondingly unique design solution. Once fully developed, each design is thoroughly documented in a set of construction drawings. Whenever possible, we stay involved with our projects through the construction process in an effort to ensure that the work is completed as planned. Biography Jonathan Chambers has more than 16 years experience in the practice of architecture. He has directed or been closely involved with the design and construction of a broad range of projects, including commercial buildings, institutional buildings, historic restorations, adaptive re-use projects, and numerous single-family residences. Jonathan received his Master of Architecture degree from Virginia Tech (1998) and his BS in Electrical Engineering from the University of Vermont (1991). During his studies, Jonathan broadened his design background by spending a semester at Virginia Tech's Center for European Studies in Riva San Vitale, Switzerland and by studying ceramics, woodworking & silk-screening. After working with another prominent Rhode Island architectural firm for a number of years, he founded Jonathan Chambers Architects in 2001. In addition to his work as an architect, Jonathan continues to design and create functional ceramic ware and ceramic jewelry. When available, his work is sold through his studio and local retailers. Commercial Architecture ​ JCA has completed a wide variety of commercial, institutional, and adaptive reuse projects in southern New England. These projects include the design of Raffa Yoga's new 12,000 SF yoga studio and active relaxation center, a new visitor's entrance and monumental staircase at the Mount Saint Charles Academy, a school children with behavioral issues, a daycare for developmentally delayed adults, a crane dealership for Shawmut Equipment, and the conversion of industrial mill buildings to loft apartments. JCA works closely with each client to see that the building we create together meets or exceeds their expectations. Our commercial work exemplifies our ability to balance functional requirements, safety concerns, and budgetary limitations with the desire to create inspirational spaces that enhance the experience of those who inhabit and interact with them. Each project is viewed as an opportunity to positively influence the built environment in which we live. Raffa Yoga In 2006, the owner of Raffa Yoga selected JCA to design her new yoga studio and active relaxation center (the first of its kind in southern New England). The owner purchased a 12,000 square foot warehouse in an industrial area. JCA assisted the owner in navigating the local zoning process to secure the approval to put a non-traditional business in an area that was zoned for manufacturing. With the proper approvals in place, JCA worked closely with the owner and her general contractor to transform the empty warehouse shell into a welcoming reception area, a boutique, a juice bar, three yoga studios, locker rooms, massage therapy rooms, heat therapy rooms, saunas, a lounge, and a steam room. The space was designed to provide an inspiring but peaceful atmosphere that supports the owner's goal of helping clientele to learn to actively relax and to be mindful. This has been one of JCA's most satisfying projects - one that we enjoy ourselves regularly and one we consistently receive positive feedback about. Residential Architecture Over the last 15 years, JCA has completed the design of more than 100 residential projects of varying scale and complexity. Working with residential clients has always been and continues to be a primary focus of our practice. We start the residential design process by listening closely to our clients thoughts about their project and observing how they interact with their current home. In addition to clearly establishing the aesthetic and functional requirements for the project, we delve deeper to determine the feel that our clients want their space to have. We use this information to create indoor and outdoor spaces that suit our clients needs and bring joy to their daily lives. Few things are more satisfying than having a client tell you that a space you designed for them has significantly affected their life in a positive way. We aim to earn those compliments on every project we undertake. Chepachet Cabin ​ The design of this screened cabin posed two substantial challenges. One, the site is an incredibly steep hillside (think double black diamond ski trail) that slopes down to the water's edge. Two, the owner wanted a sizable space for summer entertaining, but the scale of the cottage above and neighboring structures was quite small. JCA designed the cabin with two crossing gable roof lines. The end gable profile maintains the scale and proportion of the nearby homes, while masking the substantial volume inside. The entire structure is notched into the hillside, supported on two concrete retaining walls, and cantilevers out into the surrounding trees. The vertical sticking of the screened walls and the natural red cedar exterior allow the building to blend harmoniously into its surroundings. East Side Kitchen ​ The renovation and reconfiguration of the kitchen in this colonial revival home on the East Side of Providence truly exemplifies JCA’s design philosophy. The owners were not optimistic that they could have the kitchen they desired without an addition. JCA created a design that reorganized the space into an efficient, wide galley kitchen with an inviting dining nook in one corner. Circulation to adjacent rooms and the rear yard were improved for easier entertaining and improved natural lighting. Custom cabinetry by Jutras Woodworking was tailored to fit the room, maximizing storage space. A high quality result was achieved without the added expense and consumption of resources needed for an addition. This project was featured in the premiere issue of Inspired House magazine and subsequently earned a Gold Medal in Rhode Island Monthly 's Design Awards. We greatly appreciated this recognition but even more satisfying for us was the owner's feedback - that the inviting qualities of this new space draws their entire family together each evening as they prepare meals, dine, complete homework, and clean up after dinner.
